rejectionReasons: Existing daily_rollups power long-range History but retain no category membership.

Exact observation-time categoryRefs/categoryIds exist in minute_snapshots, but Twitch minute snapshots are retained for 30 days while History accepts custom ranges up to 90 days and derives previous-period comparisons.

The 90-day streamer_intraday_rollups category payload is intentionally lossy: it retains only one dominant category per streamer per hour and discards non-dominant category contributions for that hour.
Intraday streamer selection is capped after unfiltered daily ranking, so an exact selected-category filter-before-ranking result cannot be reconstructed for streamers outside that retained set.

Treating missing historical category contributions as zero, back-projecting a latest category, or presenting dominant-hour compression as exact category viewer-minutes would violate the accepted honesty boundaries.
futureReconsiderationRequirements: A separately accepted History-grade category rollup must preserve every selected-category contribution needed for the advertised metric, not only a dominant hourly category.
Category filtering must occur before category-specific ranking/capping, or the retained data must prove that omitted streamers cannot affect the requested ranking.
The retained category-aware history window must support the advertised period and any previous-period comparison without latest-category backprojection or hidden backfill.
Coverage and missing-category metadata must remain explicit at the History aggregation grain.
Any new storage, retention, backfill, collector, or D1 change requires its own governed decision and evidence before this History decision can be revisited.
nextGate: Close the Twitch History category gate as rejected on current accepted data. Parent #623 may proceed only to a separate provider-scoped decision, such as Kick category UI, while unfiltered Twitch History remains the fallback.
